facts.text: On this date in 1938, Britain and France signed the Munich Agreement, handing Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland to Hitler without consulting Czechoslovakia. The country learned its fate from a newspaper.
On this date in 1966, Botswana became independent — one of the world's poorest nations. It is now Africa's longest-running democracy and has a higher GDP per capita than Mexico.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Dhaka, Bangladesh than live outside it. That single radius captures over half of all humanity.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined — roughly 879,000 of them, holding about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
The city of Istanbul sits in two continents simultaneously. Its European side holds most of the population; its Asian side is larger in area. A commuter ferry crosses between them every 15 minutes.
On this date in 1929, the Dow Jones had already shed 20% from its September peak — weeks before the famous 'Black Tuesday' crash. The real damage was quieter, and earlier, than the legend admits.
On this date in 2008, the U.S. House rejected the first TARP bailout bill, sending the Dow down 778 points — still its largest single-day point drop at the time.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers agreeing to charge each other fixed commissions. The tree blew down in a storm. The cartel survived.
Saudi Aramco briefly held a $2 trillion market cap in 2019, making it worth more than Apple, Google, and Amazon combined at that moment. It took Apple six more years to lap it.
The Japanese government bond market is so dominated by the Bank of Japan that on some trading days, not a single bond changes hands between private investors.
On this date in 1882, Edison's first commercial power station had been running for 29 days — powered by direct current that Tesla would soon make obsolete.
On September 30, 1954, the USS Nautilus was commissioned: the first nuclear submarine, capable of running 62,000 miles on a fuel mass smaller than a golf ball.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces about 330 billion cells every day — roughly 3.8 million per second — meaning you are, in a measurable sense, always under construction.
Light takes 8 minutes to reach Earth from the Sun, but it spent up to 100,000 years fighting its way from the Sun's core to its surface before that.
On this day in 1452, the Gutenberg Bible completed printing — older than the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople, which hadn't happened yet.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
On this day in 1955, James Dean died in a car crash at 24. The film that made him immortal, Rebel Without a Cause, hadn't been released yet.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. It predates Tenochtitlán by roughly 200 years.
On this day in 1939, Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union formally divided Poland between them — the partition treaty signed just 29 days after the invasion began.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast it feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to — or one that never existed. Untranslatable, and that's precisely the point.
On this date in 1791, Mozart's opera 'The Magic Flute' premiered in Vienna. The libretto used the word 'Eingeweihten' — the initiated — a term borrowed directly from Masonic ritual.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage, yet it names something so precisely that readers swear they always knew the word.
On this date in 1955, James Dean died. The Japanese word 'mono no aware' — the bittersweet ache of impermanence — captures what his brief life became: a feeling with no English name.
On this date in 2022, Ethereum completed The Merge, switching from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake and cutting its energy use by ~99.95%. The transition happened without a single block of downtime.
On this date in 2014, Tether (then 'Realcoin') published its whitepaper. The stablecoin now settles more daily transaction volume than Visa.
Bitcoin's genesis block contains the headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but as a permanent, unalterable political statement embedded in the base layer.
The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum — it exploited a perfectly valid re-entrancy pattern in the DAO's own Solidity code. The attacker followed the rules exactly as written.
Satoshi Nakamoto's known wallet addresses hold roughly 1.1 million BTC that has never moved — making them the most-watched cold wallets in financial history, auditable by anyone in real time.
On this date in 2009, ImageNet launched publicly — the 3.2M-image dataset that made deep learning's 2012 breakthrough possible. Benchmarks shape fields more than algorithms do.
On this date in 2022, Meta released Make-A-Video, generating video from text without paired video-text training data — it learned motion from unlabeled video alone.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for ~200 million proteins in 18 months. The entire prior history of experimental biology had resolved roughly 190,000.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed more compute than all AI research published before 2012 combined — a discontinuity in kind, not degree.
The first neural net to beat humans at Go was trained partly on games it played against itself. It had never seen a professional game when it surpassed them.
